فَصِيدٌ and ↓ مَفْصُودٌ A vein slit [or opened]. (M, K.) ―
-b2- And both signify also A man bled by the opening of a vein. (TK.) ―
-b3- Also, the former, Blood (S, M, O, L, K) obtained by the cutting [or opening] of a vein (S, O, L) of a camel, (L,) and put into a gut, (S, M, O, K,) in the Time of Ignorance, (M,) and broiled: (S, M, K:) the Arabs in the Time of Ignorance used to eat it, (M, A, * L,) and to give it to the guest to eat, in a season of dearth. (S, O, * L.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
